title: Proper degree-zero Artin-Schreier map is surjective
statement: Let k be algebraically closed of prime characteristic p and f : C → Spec k a smooth proper connected curve [def-sc-curves]. Let G be an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] with natural section identifications a_U : G(U) ≃+ Γ(U,O_U), and let wp : G → G have section formula a_U(wp(x)) = a_U(x)^p-a_U(x). Then the endomorphism induced by wp on degree-zero derived etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is an epimorphism. This is only the global-functions part of the Artin-Schreier calculation, not a finiteness or field-extension assertion.

source.place: Characteristic-p branch; lem-sc-c7 proof paragraph 2; Stacks Tag 0A3P

proof.text: Smoothness implies regularity and reducedness. Put C over Spec k via f. The proper, reduced, connected global-functions theorem identifies Γ(C,O_C) with k by the structural ring map. Algebraic closedness makes x ↦ x^p-x onto k; its surjectivity transports to Γ(C,O_C) because the structural map respects powers and subtraction.

At the terminal etale object id C, the given section equivalence a and the formula hwp identify wp with that surjective ring map. Use H.equiv₀ and its naturality to prove Sheaf.H.map wp 0 is surjective. Finally the natural Ext/derived comparison conjugates this map with degree-zero derived cohomology of wp. Its component is an additive equivalence; its naturality transports the displayed surjectivity, which is epimorphy in AddCommGrpCat.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, formalized by X3 through the natural Ext/derived comparison
